definition: The quantity of purified protein, nucleic acid, or chemical product obtained from a extraction or reaction protocol.
etymology: From Old English gieldan ('to pay, produce').
manuscriptExample: Optimization of cell lysis buffers increased recombinant protein yield by 2.5-fold without compromising purity.
conferenceExample: The referee noted that RNA extraction yield was exceptionally high for degraded formalin-fixed tissue.

definition: The vertical coordinate axis in a scatter plot or bar chart, typically representing the dependent variable in data visualization.
manuscriptExample: The Y-axis represents fold-change in relative mRNA luminescence normalized to vehicle control.
conferenceExample: Reviewer 3 requested logarithmic scaling on the Y-axis to clearly display low-abundance transcript values.
